---
title: "SAS to R"
---

A practical reference for SAS programmers writing R.

Every page takes one task you already know how to do in SAS and shows how it is done
in R: the working code, its real output, and the places where the two languages do
**not** line up. The examples run when the site is built, so what you see on a page is
what R actually printed.

## How to use it

Pages are organised by what you are trying to do, not by which package provides it.
Each one opens with the SAS equivalents it replaces, so searching for `MERGE` or
`PROC TRANSPOSE` will find the right page even though nothing is filed under those names.

Code is shown in base R and the tidyverse side by side where both are worth knowing.
Where one is clearly better for the job, the page says so and explains why.

## Topics

Available now:

- [Joins](joins.qmd), combining tables

Planned, in no fixed order: data frames and tibbles, filtering and selecting, sorting,
grouping and summarising, reshaping, dates and times, text manipulation, numbers and
rounding, factors, missing data, import and export, functions and control flow,
plotting.
